original_question: Let G be a disjoint union of cycles, and let H be a disjoint union of copies of K_4. Is the graph G union H 4-colorable?
target_in_paper: Problem 3 in arXiv:2511.02892, "Strong colouring for maximum degree 2" (Penny Haxell); in formal source language, this is the "cycles plus K_4's" problem, i.e. the 2-regular specialization of Conjecture 1.3 in Dalal–McDonald–Shan.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right combinatorial objects and the right conclusion: a 2-regular graph (equivalently, a disjoint union of cycles), a disjoint union of copies of K_4, and the question of whether the resulting graph is 4-colorable. It is therefore pointed at the correct open problem family.
missing_details: The problem is not about a disjoint union of two unrelated graphs; the cycle graph and the K_4-factor must be on the same vertex set, and the operation is union of edge sets.

To make the question nontrivial and paper-faithful, the copies of K_4 should form a spanning disjoint union of K_4's on that common vertex set (equivalently, a partition of the vertex set into 4-sets, with all clique edges added inside each 4-set).
The quantifier should be explicit: for every such 2-regular graph and every such spanning K_4-factor, is the union 4-colorable?
The ambient graph class should be specified as simple graphs.
The paper's nearby formal context is strong colouring / strong chromatic number; without that context, the phrase "G union H" is easy to misread in a way that makes the problem trivial.
If one wants the exact equivalent strong-colouring formulation, one must also mention the standard padding by isolated vertices when the order is not divisible by 4.
refined_question: For every integer m >= 1, every simple 2-regular graph C on 4m vertices, and every spanning graph K on V(C) whose connected components are m vertex-disjoint copies of K_4, must the graph C ∪ K satisfy χ(C ∪ K) <= 4?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation: Does every simple graph F with maximum degree at most 2 have strong chromatic number at most 4? Explicitly, after adding 4⌈|V(F)|/4⌉ - |V(F)| isolated vertices to F, does the union with any spanning disjoint union of copies of K_4 on the enlarged vertex set always admit a proper 4-coloring?
justification: The workshop note's third problem is the cycles-plus-K_4 question in informal language. The nearest formal paper-faithful formulation is Conjecture 1.3 of Dalal–McDonald–Shan, which asks for 4-colorability after gluing vertex-disjoint K_4's onto a graph of maximum degree at most 2; they immediately note that it suffices to prove this for 2-regular base graphs, yielding exactly the cycles-only version. They also state that this is precisely the Δ=2 case of the Strong Colouring Conjecture. So the draft is aimed at the right problem, but it needs the common-vertex-set / spanning-K_4-factor interpretation made explicit; otherwise the literal reading is just a trivial disjoint union problem. I therefore kept the refined question in the narrow cycles-only form and gave the strong-colouring statement only as the single explicit equivalent formulation.
